items.title: [uv] uv's bundled CA store trusts an emSign root whose intermediate CA keys are compromised
items.summary: By default, uv verifies TLS connections against a vendored copy of the webpki-root-certs bundle. Versions before 0.13.4 include the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to that root have compromised private keys, and the CA has revoked them.An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.uv 0.13.4 removes the root from its vendored bundle, following webpki-root-certs 1.0.10. Upgrade to 0.13.4 or later.Referenceshttps://github.com/astral-sh/uv/security/advisories/GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.comhttps://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/0R3XLJL6FuE/m/0XofdebrAAAJhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62

items.title: [certifi] certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys
items.summary: Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them. An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include requests, urllib3 and pip, and the Python.org macOS installer.Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.Referenceshttps://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.comhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2
